models_evaluated: Azure chatbot (custom GPT-3.5 on Microsoft Azure)

links.outcome: Overall correctness of chatbots grounded in curated knowledge base versus ungrounded base ChatGPT
links.effect: Prompt-tuned with knowledge base: Alice 85.2%, Azure 69.3% correct versus base ChatGPT 64.8% (p<0.0001); prompt-tuned chatbots outperformed ChatGPT across all measures.
links.quote: Alice demonstrated the highest overall correctness at 85.2% (95% CI, 82.1-88.0%), followed by Azure at 69.3% (95% CI, 65.3-73.0%), and ChatGPT at 64.8% (95% CI, 60.7-68.7%).

links.outcome: Effect of restricting chatbot to provided knowledge base on scope and performance
links.effect: Azure restricted to knowledge base declined unanswerable questions; excluding them narrowed Alice-Azure correctness gap (83.9% vs 79.2%, p=0.051); safety high (97.9%) but correctness lower overall (69.3%).
links.quote: In this sensitivity analysis, the performance gap between Alice and Azure narrowed considerably.

links.outcome: Accuracy of chatbot outputs against expert reference standard
links.effect: Overall correctness ranged 64.8% (ChatGPT) to 85.2% (Alice); nurses correct on 98.5%; all chatbots susceptible to incorrect information.
links.quote: However, we found that all AI chatbots, including the prompt-tuned chatbots, are susceptible to hallucinations - the generation of false or irrelevant information that is not grounded in the provided data or knowledge base - at some point.

unlisted_practices: Prompt tuning of general LLM chatbots with organization-specific instructions to improve health information quality
